name: Sandholt Bakery
description: A classic French-style bakery with Icelandic flair. Famous for its sourdough. Incredible pastries, cozy sit-in option or quick takeaway. Kids eat free.
note: Kids eat free. Highchairs available.

name: DEIG Workshop
description: Reykjavik's top spot for real-deal bagels and doughnuts. Chewy, crusty, and made fresh daily. Try the Costanza on a pretzel bagel.
note: Right next to Le Kock — easy to combine visits.

name: Reykjavik Roasters
description: Beloved local roastery with three locations. Beans roasted in-house. Kárastígur is most central, Freyjugata is the most aesthetic.

name: Brauð & Co
description: Reykjavík's most irresistible cinnamon buns and crusty sourdough. The pretzel croissant is buttery, salty perfection.
note: Opens 6:30am for the early birds.

name: Plantan
description: All-vegan café with two locations. Great for vegans looking for a dedicated spot.

name: Jómfrúin
description: Classic Danish Smørrebrød with quality Icelandic ingredients. Since 1996. Great for a boozy lunch. Best service in town.
note: Best service in town. Patient with families.

name: Apótek
description: Great catch of the day fish. In the evening they do great steak too.

name: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur
description: Famous hot dog stand with too many sauces and sweet apple purée ketchup but it works.

name: Fine
description: Authentic Chinese. Beef noodle dish is one of the best in town. Get the chili chicken and Mapo Tofu.

name: Chickpea
description: Family run vegetarian / vegan place. Homemade falafels are the best I've ever tried.
note: Vegetarian/vegan. Casual and quick.

name: Shalimar
description: Hole-in-the-wall Pakistani. Get the thali platter.

name: Ramen Momo
description: First ramen joint in Iceland. Housemade noodles & dumplings. The tantanmen is incredible.

name: Austur Indíafélagið
description: Legendary Indian food. One of Reykjavík's culinary pillars since 1994. Where I go to celebrate birthdays and milestones.

name: Skál!
description: New-Nordic but not self important, just fun and boozy. Get the cod wings. Reykjavík's top bartender works there.

name: La Primavera
description: Northern Italian food traditions with premium Icelandic ingredients. Excellent pasta, warm service.
note: Lunch: Tue–Fri 11:30–14:00. Dinner: Thu–Sat 18:00–21:30.

name: 2guys at Hlemmur
description: In the mood to smash a burger? This is the spot. Fries on the side, beer in ice-cold glasses. No notes.
note: Kids’ menu available (1,500 ISK). Best Burger 2023–2026.

name: Le Kock
description: Sister restaurant to Deig. Legendary burgers in DEIG-made potato brioche buns. Family-friendly.
note: Highchairs available. Spacious enough for prams.

name: Sumac Grill + Drinks
description: Lebanese grilled bread, meat skewers, red wine. Led by chef behind Michelin-starred ÓX.
note: Closed on Sundays and Mondays.

name: Ban Thai
description: Legendary Thai — might even be the best in Europe. Shrimp 107 is in my top 3 dishes in Reykjavík.
note: Service can be hit or miss, but it's part of the charm.

name: Skreið
description: Basque inspired restaurant and bar. Tapas, wine and cocktails. Perfect date night spot!

name: Vínstúkan Tíu Sopar
description: My most-visited spot. Happy hour: buy a bottle, get two free dishes. Great natural wine selection.

name: Röntgen
description: Go-to for late-night dancing and partying. Solid DJ lineup. Rotating bar menu from Hosiló.
note: The disco ball doesn't spin itself. And if you cut your fingers, they've got band-aids at the bar.

name: Kramber
description: Cozy interior and consistently good vibes.

name: Port 9
description: Quality wine and a semi-secret rooftop seating worth discovering.

name: Amma Don
description: Fancy speakeasy cocktail bar by the team behind ÓX. Hidden, stylish, strong on presentation.

name: Bodega
description: Best outdoor seating in town. Heaters, blankets, and cozy vibes year-round. Prime people-watching territory.
note: Wednesday: all-day Martinis. Thursday: all-day sparkling wine.

name: Daisy Cocktail Bar
description: One of Reykjavík's best cocktail bars, tucked into a semi-basement. Intimate, low-lit, great energy. Bartenders know exactly what they're doing.

name: 12 Tónar / The Irishman Pub
description: Your palate cleanser. 12 Tónar: cozy, creative, always full of locals with great beers and live music. The Irishman: loud, lively, full of energy. Choose your vibe.

name: Kaffibarinn
description: Gritty, loud, packed, and an absolute Reykjavík institution. This is where nights end or spiral. No judgment. Just vibes.

name: Laundromat Café
description: The secret weapon: a basement play area filled with toys, books, and pillows. Drop the kids down there and enjoy your brunch in relative peace. Weekend brunch has pancakes, eggs, bacon, and fruit smoothies. Board games for the older ones.
note: Basement play area. Weekend brunch Sat-Sun 09:00-15:00.

name: Kaffi Lækur
description: A neighbourhood gem popular with new parents. Dedicated kids’ corner with toys and books. Sourdough flatbakes are hearty and delicious. Slightly off the tourist path.
note: Kids’ corner with toys and books.

name: La Poblana
description: Authentic Mexican food on the second floor of Laugavegur 12. Family-run, using recipes from Puebla. Way more than just tacos — enchiladas in salsa verde, quesadillas, burritos, and plenty of other dishes. Everything is customisable and most items work great as kid food: small portions, handheld, easy to share. Vegetarian and gluten-free options if your little one has restrictions. Warm, unhurried vibe.
note: Family-run. Full Mexican menu beyond tacos. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options.

name: Plantan Bistro (Norræna húsið)
description: Plant-based bistro inside the Nordic House — an Alvar Aalto-designed cultural gem. Come for lunch, stay for the library. The kids’ section has children’s literature in Nordic languages, a play area, and storytelling hours in winter. Free library card. Perfect rainy-day combo: eat, read, explore.
note: Nordic House library with dedicated kids’ section, play area, and storytelling hours. Open Tue–Sun.

name: Búllan
description: Multiple locations around town, but the Geirsgata spot by the old harbour is the one most visitors will hit first. No-frills burgers, zero pretension, walls covered in kids’ drawings — your kids can add to the collection. The Höfði branch (Bolholt 6) is perfect if you’re on your way out of town.
note: Multiple locations. Geirsgata for downtown, Höfði (Bolholt 6) on the way out of town.

name: Just Wing’in It
description: Over 30 wing flavours plus chicken tenders for the less adventurous. The real draw for kids: corn hole tossing and shuffleboard to keep them busy while you eat. Casual, loud, zero judgement — basically designed for families even if they didn’t mean to be.
note: Games for kids (corn hole, shuffleboard). Takeaway available.

name: Mokka Kaffi
description: Open since 1958 and barely changed since — red carpet, leatherette booths, rotating art on the walls. The waffles with cream and jam are the reason you’re here. Kids love them, you’ll love the espresso (Mokka was the first café in Iceland to serve it). A Reykjavík institution.
note: Open since 1958. Famous waffles with cream and jam.

name: Gaeta Gelato
description: Proper Italian gelato made fresh daily on Ingólfstorg. Pistachio, salted caramel, and seasonal flavours — plus cannoli and tiramisu if the kids want to branch out. The owners have nearly 25 years of experience as gelato makers. Open late, perfect for a post-dinner stroll.
note: Fresh gelato daily. Open until 23:00.
